fields.name: event_date
fields.description: Calendar date of the diagnosis-related event, derived as date of birth plus age_at_event_days. Identified counterpart to age_at_event_days. Note: rows with the -1 unknown-date sentinel yield date of birth minus one day.

fields.name: age_at_event_days
fields.description: Patient age in days at the diagnosis-related event. A value of -1 indicates an unknown date.

fields.name: metastasis
fields.description: Whether metastatic disease was present at the time of the event.

fields.name: metastasis_location
fields.description: The site of the metastasis. Semicolon-delimited when more than one site is recorded.

fields.name: metastasis_location_other
fields.description: Free-text value supplied when the coded metastasis_location does not cover the finding (the site of the metastasis).

fields.name: cns_diagnosis_category
fields.description: The diagnosis at the time of the event (broad diagnosis category).

fields.name: cns_integrated_diagnosis
fields.description: The diagnosis at the time of the event (WHO integrated histologic plus molecular diagnosis). Where CBTN recorded only a non-specific "NOS or NEC" value and a more specific molecular subtype was available from OpenPedCan for that event's biospecimen, the more specific value is shown instead; cns_integrated_diagnosis_source records which source won.

fields.name: cns_integrated_diagnosis_source
fields.description: Which source supplied cns_integrated_diagnosis on this row: 'CBTN' where the value is as CBTN recorded it, or 'OpenPedCan' where a non-specific CBTN "NOS or NEC" value was replaced by a more specific molecular subtype from openpedcan_histologies_annotated, matched on the event's biospecimen sample ID. Provenance metadata only: it carries no patient identifier and is meaningless without the diagnosis column it describes.

fields.name: tumor_locations
fields.description: The anatomical site of the tumor. Semicolon-delimited when more than one site is recorded.

fields.name: tumor_location_other
fields.description: Free-text value supplied when the coded tumor_locations does not cover the finding (the anatomical site of the tumor).

fields.name: protocol_name_and_arm
fields.description: Name of the treatment protocol the patient is enrolled on or being treated in accordance with. Sourced from the unmasked internal-use protocol name.

fields.name: protocol_name
fields.description: The protocol name alone, split from protocol_name_and_arm on its first colon. Repeats the whole value when there is no colon, so a sentinel such as Not Applicable, Not Reported or Other appears unchanged. The same trial appears both with and without an arm and all of its rows share one protocol_name, so this column can be grouped on.

fields.name: protocol_arm
fields.description: The arm, stratum or regimen within the protocol, split from protocol_name_and_arm on its first colon; any further colons are kept, for example Stratum N1: Standard Risk. Not Applicable when the value has no colon, which covers both a protocol that genuinely has no arm and a protocol that is itself unrecorded, so read protocol_name before treating this as an absence of arm.

fields.name: chemotherapy_type
fields.description: Whether the regimen followed a treatment protocol (with or without enrollment) or other standard of care.

fields.name: regimen_start_date
fields.description: Calendar date the medical therapy regimen started, derived as date of birth plus age_at_regimen_start_days. Identified counterpart to age_at_regimen_start_days. NULL when the age value is a non-numeric unknown such as 'Not Reported'.

fields.name: age_at_regimen_start_days
fields.description: Patient age in days at the start of the medical therapy regimen. May carry 'Not Reported', 'Not Available', or 'Not Applicable' for unknowns.

fields.name: regimen_stop_date
fields.description: Calendar date the medical therapy regimen ended, derived as date of birth plus age_at_regimen_stop_days. Identified counterpart to age_at_regimen_stop_days. NULL when the age value is a non-numeric unknown such as 'Not Reported'.

fields.name: age_at_regimen_stop_days
fields.description: Patient age in days at the end of the medical therapy regimen. May carry 'Not Reported', 'Not Available', or 'Not Applicable' for unknowns.

fields.name: chemotherapy_agents
fields.description: Therapeutic agent being administered. Sourced from the unmasked internal-use agent list.

fields.name: is_initial_treatment
fields.description: yes/no column indicating whether this regimen was part of the patient's initial treatment (the treatment that occurred prior to the first relapse, progression, second malignancy, or death). 'no' also covers rows where this could not be determined. Derived from ages in days only, so it exposes no calendar date.

fields.description: True when you may read this patient's PHI (MRN and calendar dates); dates are empty otherwise.

fields.name: wbc_value
fields.description: Latest WBC result value. NOT unit-normalized - read with its unit; the same analyte arrives in incompatible units across contributing systems.

fields.name: wbc_source_code_text
fields.description: Local result name as recorded by the contributing system for the WBC observation, retained verbatim for provenance.

fields.name: anc_observed_at

fields.name: protein_display
fields.description: Most recent CSF total protein pre-composed as comparator + value + unit, e.g. '<10 mg/dL'. READ THIS RATHER THAN protein_value: the comparator is load-bearing and a '<' result is below the assay limit, not a measurement. Each component is resolved to ITS OWN most recent result, so this may come from a different lumbar puncture than the other components - compare the paired dates or ages before treating two components as contemporaneous.

fields.name: protein_value
fields.description: Numeric CSF total protein WITHOUT its comparator. Do not read in isolation - see protein_display.

fields.name: protein_comparator
fields.description: Comparator attached to protein_value, typically '<' or '>' when the result is outside the assay's reportable range; NULL for an absolute measurement.

fields.name: protein_unit
fields.description: Unit of measure for protein_value; uniformly mg/dL for this analyte.

fields.name: protein_observed_at
fields.description: Calendar timestamp of the most recent CSF total protein (UTC), from DiagnosticReport.effective_date_time - a genuine clinical date. Identified counterpart to age_at_protein_days. Each component is resolved to ITS OWN most recent result, so this may come from a different lumbar puncture than the other components - compare the paired dates or ages before treating two components as contemporaneous.

fields.name: age_at_protein_days
fields.description: Patient age in days at the most recent CSF total protein. De-identified counterpart to protein_observed_at. NULL precisely when the component is absent, so a NULL age means the test was not done rather than the age being unknown. Comparing this against another component's age reveals whether the two came from the same puncture without exposing either date.

fields.name: protein_source_code_text

fields.name: wbc_display

fields.name: wbc_unit
fields.description: Unit of measure for wbc_value. Six equivalent spellings occur; the value is comparable across all of them without conversion.

fields.name: wbc_source_code_text

fields.name: rbc_source_code_text

fields.name: cytology_evidence_tier
fields.description: How this specific cytology result was attributed to CSF: 'named' (report name states CSF), 'text_confirmed' (the result text states CSF and no competing source), or 'same_day_only' (no source stated, but CSF was drawn that day - weakest). Necessary because no specimen-to-report link exists.

fields.name: cytology_test_name
fields.description: Local order name of the most recent CSF cytology as recorded by the contributing system, retained verbatim for provenance.

fields.name: malignant_cells
fields.description: DERIVED finding classified from the cytology narrative: positive, suspicious, negative, non_diagnostic, no_malignancy_statement, or NULL where no narrative exists. Deliberately visible to all callers as the de-identified stand-in for the gated free text - a clinical finding, not an identifier. A deterministic keyword classifier with three negation passes, so treat it as a screening aid and confirm against cytology_final_diagnosis for case-by-case use.

fields.name: multi_specimen_report
fields.description: 1 when the underlying report covered more than one specimen, so the malignant_cells finding may pertain to a non-CSF part and needs confirmation. Read alongside malignant_cells; suppressing this flag while showing the label would present a reviewable inference as settled fact.

fields.name: cytology_final_diagnosis
fields.description: The pathologist's Final Diagnosis / Impression for the most recent CSF cytology, verbatim. FREE CLINICAL TEXT CONTAINING PHI: the specimen label quoted in these reports includes the patient name and medical record number. Gated behind PHI access and masked whole - there is no partial or redacted form. Non-PHI callers get malignant_cells instead.

fields.name: cytology_result_text
fields.description: All diagnostic narrative sections of the most recent CSF cytology report stitched together, verbatim. FREE CLINICAL TEXT CONTAINING PHI - patient name, medical record number and provider names appear. Gated behind PHI access and masked whole. Up to 10,805 characters; assembled once when the base table was materialised under a raised group_concat_max_len, since the 1024-byte default truncates silently.

fields.name: cytology_observed_at
fields.description: Calendar timestamp of the most recent CSF cytology (UTC). Identified counterpart to age_at_cytology_days. Each component is resolved to ITS OWN most recent result, so this may come from a different lumbar puncture than the other components - compare the paired dates or ages before treating two components as contemporaneous.

fields.name: age_at_cytology_days
fields.description: Patient age in days at the most recent CSF cytology. De-identified counterpart to cytology_observed_at; NULL precisely when no cytology exists.

fields.name: afp_display

READ THIS RATHER THAN afp_value: the comparator is on the MAJORITY of these results and '<' means UNDETECTABLE, not a concentration at the limit. Each component is resolved to ITS OWN most recent result, so this may come from a different lumbar puncture than the other components - compare the paired dates or ages before treating two components as contemporaneous.

fields.name: afp_value
fields.description: Numeric CSF alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) WITHOUT its comparator. Reading it alone reports an undetectable marker as a real concentration - see afp_display.

fields.name: afp_comparator
fields.description: Comparator attached to afp_value, '<' for an undetectable marker; NULL when the value is a genuine measurement, which is the case for the clinically elevated results.

fields.name: afp_unit
fields.description: Unit of measure for afp_value. Not normalised - AFP appears as both 'ng/mL' and 'NG/ML'.

fields.name: afp_observed_at
fields.description: Calendar timestamp of the most recent CSF alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) (UTC). Identified counterpart to age_at_afp_days. Each component is resolved to ITS OWN most recent result, so this may come from a different lumbar puncture than the other components - compare the paired dates or ages before treating two components as contemporaneous.

fields.name: age_at_afp_days
fields.description: Patient age in days at the most recent CSF alpha-fetoprotein (AFP). De-identified counterpart to afp_observed_at; NULL precisely when the marker was never measured.

fields.name: hcg_display

READ THIS RATHER THAN hcg_value: the comparator is on the MAJORITY of these results and '<' means UNDETECTABLE, not a concentration at the limit. Each component is resolved to ITS OWN most recent result, so this may come from a different lumbar puncture than the other components - compare the paired dates or ages before treating two components as contemporaneous.

fields.name: hcg_comparator

fields.name: hcg_unit

fields.name: hcg_observed_at
fields.description: Calendar timestamp of the most recent CSF beta-hCG (UTC). Identified counterpart to age_at_hcg_days. Each component is resolved to ITS OWN most recent result, so this may come from a different lumbar puncture than the other components - compare the paired dates or ages before treating two components as contemporaneous.

fields.name: age_at_hcg_days

fields.name: cea_observed_at

fields.name: age_at_cea_days

fields.name: cell_free_dna_observed_at

fields.name: age_at_cell_free_dna_days

fields.name: age_at_malignant_cell_panel_days

fields.name: pathology_review_text

fields.name: pathology_review_observed_at
fields.description: Calendar timestamp of the most recent pathologist review of the CSF differential (UTC). Identified counterpart to age_at_pathology_review_days.

fields.name: age_at_pathology_review_days
fields.description: Patient age in days at the most recent pathologist review of the CSF differential. De-identified counterpart to pathology_review_observed_at.

fields.name: components_present
fields.description: Count of the eleven CSF components that resolved for this patient (1-11). A completeness indicator, not clinical content.

fields.name: csf_reports_total
fields.description: Total distinct CSF reports contributing to this row across all components.

fields.name: first_csf_result_at
fields.description: Calendar timestamp of the patient's EARLIEST CSF result of any component (UTC). Identified counterpart to age_at_first_csf_result_days.

fields.name: age_at_first_csf_result_days
fields.description: Patient age in days at the earliest CSF result of any component. With age_at_last_csf_result_days it gives the span of CSF surveillance without exposing either date.

fields.name: last_csf_result_at
fields.description: Calendar timestamp of the patient's LATEST CSF result of any component (UTC). Identified counterpart to age_at_last_csf_result_days.

fields.name: age_at_last_csf_result_days

This is the vocabulary auth.pii_grant keys on; NULL for 6 of 814 patients, who consequently fail closed to de-identified with their free text hidden. 190 patients resolve to SCH, the org currently granted for tenant cbtn, so this view does release identified values and clinical text to the current grant holder.

fields.name: patient_id
fields.description: Patient identifier: the medical record number (MRN) when you may read this patient's PHI, otherwise the research id. Same value in every entity, so it links them.

fields.name: patient_id_type
fields.description: Which identifier patient_id holds: mrn or research_id.

fields.name: radiant_patient_id
fields.description: Portal surrogate patient key (radiant_jdbc.public.patient.id), joined on organization_code plus MRN with leading zeros stripped from both sides because the portal zero-pads to a fixed width and pcx_30 does not. NULL when the patient has no portal record, which is the common case: the portal currently holds cbtn patients for SCH only. Deliberately projected to every caller rather than gated behind can_read_phi, unlike patient_fhir_id in the other views -- it is treated as a non-identifying surrogate. Note it does resolve to a portal record carrying name, date of birth and MRN, so it is a re-linking key for anyone who can also reach that table.

fields.name: patient_best_evidence
fields.description: Strongest evidence anywhere for this patient that the analysis was on CSF: 'named' (a report name states CSF), 'text_confirmed' (the result text states CSF and no competing source), or 'same_day_only' (no source stated; CSF drawn the same day). Filter to 'named' for the strictly defensible subset. No specimen-to-report link exists in the source data, which is why this tiering is necessary.

fields.name: evidence_tier
fields.description: Evidence tier of THE RETURNED (most recent) analysis specifically, same vocabulary as patient_best_evidence. Can be weaker than patient_best_evidence: a patient's best-evidenced analysis is not necessarily their latest.

fields.name: latest_test_family
fields.description: Which tumour-relevant CSF assay the most recent analysis was: cytology, tumor_marker_afp, tumor_marker_hcg, tumor_marker_cea, cell_free_dna, malignant_cell_panel, or pathology_review.

fields.name: latest_test_name
fields.description: Local order name of the most recent analysis as recorded by the contributing system, retained verbatim for provenance.

fields.name: latest_analyzed_at
fields.description: Calendar timestamp of the most recent CSF analysis, from DiagnosticReport.effective_date_time (UTC). Identified counterpart to age_at_latest_analysis_days. A genuine clinical date, 100% populated for these reports.

fields.name: age_at_latest_analysis_days
fields.description: Patient age in days at the most recent CSF analysis, derived from date of birth. De-identified counterpart to latest_analyzed_at. Exact to the day and reaching ~59 years, so not automatically anonymous when combined with a known diagnosis. Populated for all 814 rows.

fields.name: malignant_cells
fields.description: DERIVED finding classified from the pathology narrative: positive, suspicious, negative, non_diagnostic, no_malignancy_statement, or NULL where the analysis carries no narrative (mostly quantitative markers). Deliberately visible to all callers as the de-identified stand-in for the gated free text - it is a clinical finding, not an identifier. A deterministic keyword classifier with negation handling, so treat it as a screening aid and confirm against final_diagnosis for case-by-case use.

fields.name: multi_specimen_report
fields.description: 1 when the underlying report covered more than one specimen, so the malignant_cells finding may pertain to a non-CSF part and needs confirmation. Read alongside malignant_cells; suppressing this flag while showing the label would present a reviewable inference as settled fact.

fields.name: result_display
fields.description: Quantitative result pre-composed as comparator + value + unit, e.g. '<1.0 ng/mL'. READ THIS RATHER THAN result_value: the comparator is load-bearing, and most tumour-marker results are '<' i.e. UNDETECTABLE. Dropping it would report an undetectable marker as a real concentration.

fields.name: result_value
fields.description: Numeric quantitative result WITHOUT its comparator. Do not read in isolation - see result_display. Units are not normalised.

fields.name: result_comparator
fields.description: Comparator attached to result_value, typically '<' for an undetectable marker, NULL when the value is an absolute measurement.

fields.name: result_unit
fields.description: Unit of measure for result_value (ng/mL for AFP, IU/L for beta-hCG). NOT normalised - both 'ng/mL' and 'NG/ML' occur.

fields.name: final_diagnosis
fields.description: The pathologist's Final Diagnosis / Impression section, verbatim. Gated behind PHI access in the tenant view and masked whole - there is no partial or redacted form. Non-PHI callers get malignant_cells instead.

fields.name: result_text
fields.description: All diagnostic narrative sections of the report stitched together (Final Diagnosis, Impression, Microscopic Description, Gross Description, Clinical Information and others), verbatim. FREE CLINICAL TEXT CONTAINING PHI - patient name, medical record number and provider names appear. Gated behind PHI access and masked whole. Up to 10,805 characters; assembled once when the base table was materialised under a raised group_concat_max_len, since the 1024-byte default truncates silently.

fields.name: result_sections
fields.description: Count of narrative sections that carried text for the most recent analysis. A structural count, not clinical content.

fields.name: csf_analyses_total
fields.description: Total tumour-relevant CSF analyses recorded for this patient across all evidence tiers, not just the most recent one.

fields.name: first_analyzed_at
fields.description: Calendar timestamp of the patient's EARLIEST tumour-relevant CSF analysis. Identified counterpart to age_at_first_analysis_days.

fields.name: distinct_families
fields.description: Count of distinct tumour-relevant assay families recorded for this patient (1-7).

fields.name: families_ever
fields.description: Comma-separated list of every tumour-relevant CSF assay family recorded for this patient, so a caller can see that e.g. both AFP and beta-hCG were done without reading per-analysis rows.

fields.name: can_read_phi

lansky_karnofsky_latest.description: Latest Lansky or Karnofsky performance status score per patient.

fields.name: organization_name
fields.description: Name of the institution that contributed the patient's data, from stg_cbtn_enrollment_final.

fields.name: organization_code
fields.description: Short code for the contributing institution, from pcx_30_organization_ref. This is the vocabulary auth.pii_grant keys on; NULL for 14 of 1,627 patients, who consequently fail closed to de-identified. No patient in this view resolves to SCH, the only org currently granted for tenant cbtn, so every current grant holder sees a fully de-identified result.

fields.name: patient_id
fields.description: Patient identifier: the medical record number (MRN) when you may read this patient's PHI, otherwise the research id. Same value in every entity, so it links them.

fields.name: patient_id_type
fields.description: Which identifier patient_id holds: mrn or research_id.

fields.name: radiant_patient_id
fields.description: Portal surrogate patient key (radiant_jdbc.public.patient.id), joined on organization_code plus MRN with leading zeros stripped from both sides because the portal zero-pads to a fixed width and pcx_30 does not. Currently NULL on every row: this view's patient set has no overlap with the portal's, which holds cbtn patients for SCH only. Deliberately projected to every caller rather than gated behind can_read_phi, unlike patient_fhir_id in the other views -- it is treated as a non-identifying surrogate. Note it does resolve to a portal record carrying name, date of birth and MRN, so it is a re-linking key for anyone who can also reach that table.

fields.name: scale
fields.description: Which performance-status instrument produced the score: 'lansky' (pediatric) or 'karnofsky' (adult). One row per patient, carrying whichever scale was recorded most recently, so a patient who transitioned between instruments appears under the later one only.

fields.name: score
fields.description: Performance-status score, 10-100 where higher is better function. Parsed from the leading number of the source free-text answer; observed values land on 10-100 in steps of ten. Lansky and Karnofsky are NOT interchangeable scales - read with the scale column.

fields.name: scored_at
fields.description: Calendar timestamp of the score, from Observation.issued, in UTC. Identified counterpart to age_at_score_days. This is a result-release time, not the assessment time: both FHIR clinical date columns are unpopulated for these two scales. NULL for 104 of 1,627 patients for whom no date exists upstream at all.

fields.name: age_at_score_days
fields.description: Patient age in days at the score, derived from date of birth. De-identified counterpart to scored_at. Exact to the day and reaching ~35 years, so not automatically anonymous when combined with a known diagnosis. NULL for the 104 patients with no scored_at - unlike the other views here, the age is not an always-present substitute for the gated timestamp, so those rows cannot be placed in time by any means.

fields.name: score_text
fields.description: Source free-text answer the score was parsed from, e.g. '90 - Minor restrictions in strenuous activity', retained verbatim so the parse is auditable. Describes function only and carries no patient identifier.

fields.name: scale_code
fields.description: Coded identity of the instrument as recorded by the source system: EPIC#1501 (Lansky) or MEDCIN#124024 (Karnofsky). Used to select these observations in preference to the verbose local code_text.

fields.name: source_code_text
fields.description: Local observation name as recorded by the contributing system, retained verbatim for provenance.

fields.name: component_line
fields.description: Source flowsheet line label ('Line 1' to 'Line 4') the score was read from. Where one observation carries more than one scored line (75 of 42,380), the lowest line wins.

fields.name: date_semantic
fields.description: How this row's date was obtained: 'administrative' (from Observation.issued, a release-time proxy) or 'undated' (no date exists upstream). Never 'clinical' in this view - no clinical-dated alternative exists for these two scales.

fields.name: can_read_phi
fields.description: True when you may read this patient's PHI (MRN and calendar dates); dates are empty otherwise.
